<reason>Side A won on the strength of the behavioral-evidence core: shrinkflation exists as a strategy precisely because gram counts go unread at the moment of purchase, and B's own concession in [B2.2] that firms shrink to preserve price points shoppers anchor on handed A the asymmetry he needed. A's answer to the memory question ([B3.1]) was the sharpest turn of the debate: the firm itself is betting the sticker is noticed and the grams are not, so the two disclosures cannot be treated as equally visible. B landed real counterpunches — the delta-mixing problem ([B3.2]) was genuinely damaging, and B's Rebuttal 2 tracked A's repairs (safe harbours, split deltas, flagged increases, "was $3.49" tags) into a convincing "regime creep" narrative. But A's responses held: showing two lines answers the misleading-number charge, and the weighing that drafting details are regulator work, not grounds for leaving shoppers in the dark, was cleaner than B's final "fine print cannot be rescued by more of it," which sat awkwardly beside B's earlier claim that the information is already plainly disclosed. B also never squarely resolved the tension between "plain ink tells shoppers everything" and "shoppers can't detect either change without memory." A's repeated unanswered question about whether any mandated disclosure is acceptable was only belatedly answered in B's closing. Both sides were disciplined, grounded in plausible background knowledge, and free of fake precision; A simply made the decisive clash easier to decide.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>The exchange over memory and visibility: B pressed that detecting a sticker increase requires memory just like detecting a gram change ([B3.1]), and A's reply ([A4.1]) — that when the sticker moves the shopper is reading the changed number and can compare rivals on the same shelf, while a gram change hides behind an identical sticker — turned B's own price-point-anchoring concession into the decisive asymmetry. B's best counter, the delta-mixing question, was solidly answered by A's two-line display, though B's framing of it as regime creep kept the point alive to the end.</best_rebuttal>
